docs.title: AtomicNG
docs.text:
AtomicNG implements atomic, forward-only continual writes to a language model's n-gram memory. It follows the method described in arXiv:2610.31125 (Hao Wu) — an independent implementation, not affiliated with the author; reference code lives at af-74413592/delta-ngram. The pretrained n-gram hash table T⁰ stays frozen, and writes accumulate in a sparse patch Δ such that T = T⁰ + Δ. Write guards enforce budgets and caps before the patch changes. Clearing Δ restores the base model bit for bit.

The Apache-2.0 core uses NumPy. The optional PyTorch layer provides writers and Hugging Face integration. See the vLLM integration guide for the general plugin.

CPU, CUDA, and TPU calibration results · Run TPU calibration in Colab

docs.title: Try the CPU demo
docs.text:
python -m pip install atomicng==1.0.0

Run the following with Python. It uses the deterministic NumPy test backend and needs no model download or GPU. The matching probe and eight neutral probes are measured separately.

import atomicng

model = atomicng.TinyModel()
writer = atomicng.HashWriter(model.spec)
text = "A field note about volcanic soil chemistry."
query = writer.tokenize(text)

before = model.logits(query).tobytes()
report = atomicng.write(model, text, writer=writer)
written = model.logits(query).tobytes()
assert report.n_rows > 0 and written != before
print(f"Write: {report.n_rows} rows touched. Matching probe changed.")

neutral = model.neutral_token_seqs(8)
neutral_written = model.run_seqs(neutral).tobytes()
atomicng.clear_memory(model)

assert model.logits(query).tobytes() == before
assert model.run_seqs(neutral).tobytes() == neutral_written
print("Clear: matching probe restored byte for byte.")
print("Control: eight neutral probes unchanged.")

The example measures probe outputs. For writer training on a Hugging Face model, see the calibration results.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
pip install -e .            # Core dependencies: NumPy and PyYAML
pip install -e ".[torch]"   # Writers and Hugging Face backend
pip install -e ".[dev]"     # Development and test dependencies

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
import atomicng

model = atomicng.TinyModel()  # Local test backend
policies = atomicng.WritePolicies(row_budget=100_000, hot_row_norm_cap=1.0)
metrics, audit, undo = atomicng.MetricsRegistry(), atomicng.AuditLog("audit.jsonl"), atomicng.UndoJournal()

report = atomicng.write(
    model, "A document containing a new fact...",
    policies=policies, metrics=metrics, audit=audit, undo=undo, source="doc-1",
)
model.memory.save_pretrained("out.atomicng.npz")  # Data-only overlay and SHA-256 manifest
atomicng.publish_check(model)  # Checks verification, drift, and hot rows

The Hugging Face backend uses atomicng.backends.hf.attach_sidecar. The CLI reads YAML configurations from configs/.

atomicng write --evidence docs.txt --overlay mem.atomicng.npz --config configs/write_default.yaml
atomicng stats mem.atomicng.npz          # Rows, norms, reuse, and provenance
atomicng verify mem.atomicng.npz         # Check the SHA-256 integrity manifest
atomicng merge --base a.atomicng.npz --other b.atomicng.npz --out c.atomicng.npz
atomicng publish mem.atomicng.npz --config configs/publish_strict.yaml
atomicng bench --save baseline.json && atomicng bench --docs 200 --check baseline.json
atomicng eval --evidence examples/eval_docs.txt --suite quick --json report.json
atomicng monitor mem.atomicng.npz --metrics m.jsonl            # Standalone HTML report
atomicng export-ple --overlay mem.atomicng.npz --out table.ple  # Table for llama.cpp
atomicng smoke

docs.title: Write safety and integrity
docs.text: Mechanism Behavior Immutable base table Writes affect only the sparse Δ store. Atomic guards Row and write budgets and hard caps are checked before the patch changes. Write report Each write reports rows, gates, norms, and hot-row flags. Exact undo atomicng.revert_last restores the last block from its pre-image journal. LIFO only: exact for the most recent block; older blocks whose rows were touched later cannot be reverted exactly (D1 depends on current row state). Full reset model.memory.clear() removes the full patch. Overlay integrity The format stores data only (NPZ and JSON) with a SHA-256 manifest. Publication checks Verification must pass, and drift and hot-row counts must stay within their limits. Audit An append-only JSONL log records writes and merges with checksums.

docs.title: Monitoring
docs.text: MetricsRegistry supports JSONL and optional TensorBoard and Weights & Biases exporters. It records gates, patch norms, hot rows, row reuse, and events per second, both per write and in aggregate.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
src/atomicng/
├── specs.py        # Versioned table specifications and validation
├── memory.py       # Sparse patch, lazy decay, merge, and overlay integrity
├── guards.py       # Atomic write budgets and caps
├── rules/d1.py     # Two-phase D1 block averaging
├── evidence.py     # Document blocks (512/128) and ByteTokenizer
├── metrics.py      # Metrics registry and exporters
├── bench.py        # Throughput, overhead, and regression checks
├── publishing.py   # Verification, drift, and hot-row checks
├── journal.py      # Audit log and pre-image undo
├── verify.py       # Bit-exact deletion checks on neutral probes
├── backends/       # Tiny CPU backend and Hugging Face sidecar hooks
└── writers/        # Plain/delta WriterMLP and BPTT through the D1 update chain

The core runs without PyTorch. Writer training and the Hugging Face sidecar require the torch extra. Full JAX model attachment is roadmap work.

docs.title: Tests
docs.text:
python tests/run_all.py        # Or run pytest -q
ruff check src tests

The suite covers D1, gates, Eq. 7, writer parameters, and ρ calibration, along with plain encoding, safetensors writer artifacts, Ed25519 signatures, HTML monitoring, PLE export, and the PyTorch layer. Hugging Face integration tests exercise attaching, writing to, and clearing the sidecar on a tiny random Llama model. See FIDELITY.md and pytest tests/test_fidelity.py.

docs.title: Use the pretrained SmolLM2-135M Writer
docs.text:
The 860-step Writer checkpoint is publicly downloadable. Run the CPU example from this checkout to download and verify the checkpoint, load the pinned SmolLM2-135M base model, and check a forward-only write and bit-exact rollback.

python -m pip install "atomicng[torch]==1.0.0" transformers
python examples/pretrained_writer.py

The checkpoint contains Writer weights. The example initializes a reproducible sidecar projection because the original run did not save its projection. The example reports the measured NLL on one input alongside the write and rollback checks. See the calibration record for the original training results.

Checkpoint NLL audit (fixed seed, script, run on the shipped 860-step checkpoint):

Measurement Result Held-out doc, written doc itself (before → after write) ≈ 0 (max +0.0033) — acquisition sanity check only Paraphrase of the written doc (before → after) −0.09 … −2.05 (mean −0.89): memory writes currently HURT paraphrases Unrelated held-out text (before → after 8 writes) exactly 0.0 — perfect locality

The paraphrase damage is hash-collision interference: rows written for the doc's bigrams fire inside the paraphrase with deltas derived from a different context. This is the real limit at this training scale — the paper's writer (100M training tokens) resolves it. Multi-seed retraining is queued.

docs.title: Train a writer on your own model
docs.text:
python scripts/train_writer.py --model HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-135M \
    --corpus corpus.txt --out runs/demo --steps 30

The model stays frozen while training updates the writer (approximately 50,000 to 4 million parameters). The CPU configuration uses block length/stride 96/24. The GPU configuration uses 512/128, as in the paper. The example writes runs/demo/writer.safetensors with provenance and runs/demo/eval.json with per-document Δ_empty.

docs.title: Release checks
docs.text:
The build job creates a source distribution and wheel, and checks them with Twine. The core CI job runs atomicng smoke; release validation also recorded a smoke pass against a wheel installed in a clean environment. The quickstart notebook provides runnable examples. The Docker image uses python:3.12-slim and runs the smoke check during the build.

See the changelog for release history and the release checklist for publication steps.

docs.title: Linux CUDA verification for 0.4.0a3
docs.text:
• The Tesla T4 run on Python 3.13 passed 72 of 72 tests. The acquisition check avoided rounding and the publication gate used self-contained YAML.
  • The CUDA path exercised attach, write, and NLL evaluation. Clearing Δ restored outputs bit for bit (max_diff = 0.0) with deterministic CUDA mode and CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG.

docs.title: SmolLM2-135M writer training
docs.text:
The sidecar used a 4096×16 table and seed 17.

Run Steps Loss Acquisition Δ_empty Kaggle CPU, 7.8 h 860 3.36 → 3.12 (min 1.606) +0.0422 on document 1, 0 on the others Colab TPU VM, 45 min (run 1) 157 3.36 → ~2.7–3.4 (min 1.6025) −0.0272 to 0 Colab TPU VM, 45 min (run 2) 156 3.35 → ~2.4–3.4 (min 1.6116) −0.0173 to +0.0147 (mean +0.0024)

These runs exercised the end-to-end training path. The longest run showed a positive acquisition signal on one document. Reproducing the paper's 100-million-token training regime remains separate work.

docs.title: Shipped checkpoint NLL audit (fixed seed, 2026-11-12)
docs.text:
Measured on the released 860-step checkpoint against held-out Sherlock paragraphs (script):

Measurement Δ (NLL before → after write) Held-out doc, the written doc itself ≈ 0 (max +0.0033) — acquisition sanity check only Paraphrase of the written doc −0.09 … −2.05 (mean −0.89): writes currently HURT paraphrases Unrelated held-out text after 8 writes exactly 0.0 — perfect locality

The paraphrase damage is hash-collision interference: rows written for the doc's bigrams fire inside the paraphrase carrying deltas derived from a different context. At this training scale it is the dominant effect; the paper's writer (100M training tokens) resolves it. Multi-seed retraining is queued.

docs.title: TPU results
docs.text:
• On Kaggle TPU VM, the XLA BPTT chain reached S3 on device. The session was canceled after two hours.
  • On Colab v5e with Python 3.13 and PyTorch 2.14.1, JAX 0.11.2 detected the TPU. The PyPI torch_xla build had an ABI mismatch with the preinstalled PyTorch (_XLAC.so: undefined symbol). The notebook includes a cell to install a matching pair and restart the runtime.
  • On 5 November, the owner ran S3b on TPU_0 with JAX. The D1 read, writer, and write loop took 8.4 ms/iteration. The maximum was 0.156 s, including first-iteration JIT compilation. Loss stayed finite across 20 iterations. The recorded report is kaggle-evidence/colab-tpu/results/S3b_accel_jax.json.
  • The notebook's XLA path is used for on-device BPTT training after restarting with the matching packages.

docs.title: vLLM on Kaggle Linux and Tesla T4
docs.text:
• export_for_vllm generated ngram_table_merged.npz and vllm_config.json with SHA-256 and provenance on the target platform.
  • vLLM generated text with facebook/opt-125m at 21.4 output tokens/s on a T4. AtomicNG artifacts were present in the same environment. An isolated uv virtual environment avoided the conflict with Kaggle's preinstalled PyTorch. See kaggle-night-vllm/verify_vllm3.py.
  • Loading the merged table into the engine graph remains Track B upstream work. See the vLLM integration guide.

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• Bit-exact CUDA restoration requires deterministic mode. CPU restoration does not require those flags.
  • The XLA path keeps bigram hashing on the CPU behind a gradient stop and places the tensors on the TPU.
  • The vLLM reader has yet to be calibrated.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: AtomicNG follows Keep a Changelog and Semantic Versioning.

docs.title: Fixed (fidelity review by the method author, issue #1 on the reference repo)
docs.text:
• c_j counts BLOCKS, not events: D1 averages a block's events into one update, so the counter grows by 1 per writing block (previously += n_j per event). Affects the gate input log(1 + c_j). Fixed in rules/d1.py and both trainers; the count test now asserts the block semantics (1 per block, 2 after two blocks).
  • Undo is LIFO: documented in journal.py and README — exact for the most recent block; older blocks whose rows were touched later cannot be reverted exactly.
  • Sidecar projection ships with writer checkpoints (save_sidecar_proj / load_sidecar_proj) — published writers are reproducible end-to-end (projection deterministic from seed 17).
  • CALIBRATION.md: SmolLM2 results explicitly labeled external-table setup; acquisition reported as Δ_empty + Δ_donor pairs (forgetting can raise Δ_donor).
  • README: explicit independent-implementation statement.

docs.title: [1.0.0] — 2026-11-05
docs.text: First stable release. A golden test freezes the public API.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• NumPy core for T = T⁰ + Δ, with D1 block averaging, atomic write guards, pre-image undo, full reset, and data-only overlays with SHA-256 and Ed25519 support.
  • Plain and delta MLP writers, with BPTT through the D1 update chain on PyTorch CPU, CUDA, and XLA paths.
  • Track B native read-out in native.py (16 heads × 160 dimensions, followed by value and gated key paths with 10,240 output dimensions).
  • A vllm.general_plugins entry point, merged-table export for vLLM, and PLE export for llama.cpp.
  • Acquisition, distraction, and chain evaluations, with 512-token evidence blocks and a 128-token query prefix.
  • Write reports, metrics exporters, standalone HTML monitoring, regression checks, publication checks, and an audit log.
  • Documentation, a Colab TPU notebook, and core, PyTorch, build, and publication workflows.

docs.title: Recorded validation
docs.text:
• 85 of 85 tests on Windows and 72 of 72 on Linux with CUDA T4 and Python 3.13. The CUDA run verified bit-exact restoration after clearing Δ.
  • The 860-step SmolLM2-135M writer run recorded acquisition Δ_empty = +0.0422 on one document.
  • The JAX D1 harness recorded 8.4 ms/iteration on TPU_0. See CALIBRATION.md for the run conditions and limits.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• MkDocs Material documentation and a GitHub Pages workflow. scripts/build_docs.py assembles the site from the repository Markdown.
  • test_api_surface freezes __all__, reports added and removed names, and requires intentional changes to be documented.
  • Examples and a release checklist covering PyPI, the Colab TPU run, and vLLM validation.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • Stabilized test_trainer_d1_chain_is_bptt with deterministic blocks and the trainer's guard for groups without a gradient path.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• The atomicng_ngram_overlay general plugin reads VLLM_ATOMICNG_OVERLAY and exposes a provider for T⁰+Δ. It returns an empty mapping when no overlay is configured and does not import vLLM.
  • atomicng export-vllm writes a merged NPZ table and vllm_config.json with SHA-256 and provenance. The integration guide documents three paths and includes an upstream issue draft.
  • Six bridge tests cover merge behavior, environment configuration, export artifacts, and the entry point.
  • README badges, the calibration matrix, and a direct Colab link.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Track B native adapter primitives in native.py. NativeTableSpec defines eight bigram heads and eight trigram heads of width 160. native_head_rows and native_rows_all_heads compute row addresses. NativeReadOut concatenates rows into ℝ²⁵⁶⁰ and applies value and gated key paths to produce ℝ¹⁰²⁴⁰. The key path uses RMSNorm, a signed square-root transform with a floor, and four-tap causal depthwise convolution with dilation 3.
  • Recorded calibration across Windows CPU, Kaggle CPU, CUDA T4 (73 ms/group), Colab 24-core CPU (54 ms/group, preliminary), and TPU. The 860-step CPU run recorded acquisition of +0.0422.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Skip backpropagation for groups without a gradient path in WriterTrainer.train_group. The BPTT test now uses deterministic blocks with repeated rows.
  • Convert NumPy patch values to tensors in test_gather_uses_memory.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Place SidecarHandle.forward_hidden token IDs on the model device, move CUDA tensors to CPU before calling .numpy() in SidecarTable.read(), and place injected reads on the projection device.
  • Keep full precision in acquisition results so comparison with NLL differences avoids double rounding.
  • Make test_publish_gate use a self-contained YAML file in its temporary directory.

docs.title: Recorded validation
docs.text:
• The initial Kaggle T4 run recorded BPTT loss 5.55 → 4.05 at 73 ms/group and passed 70 of 72 tests. This release addressed both failures.
  • Kaggle CPU recorded 860 SmolLM2-135M writer steps in 7.8 hours, loss 3.36 → 3.12 (min 1.606), acquisition Δ_empty = +0.0422, and 71 of 72 tests passing.
  • The TPU run exercised on-device XLA BPTT. The session was canceled after about two hours, with S0–S4 artifacts collected.

docs.title: Added
docs.text: • Device support for HFWriterTrainer(..., device=...) and SidecarTable.to(device). The trainer places the model, writer, sidecar table, and training tensors on the selected device.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • Create SidecarHandle.nll indices on the input device for CUDA compatibility.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Source and wheel builds, Twine checks, and a smoke check against a wheel installed in a clean environment. The CI build job checks package artifacts.
  • A quickstart notebook, a Python 3.12 slim Docker image with a build-time smoke check, and a Docker ignore file.
  • Write-time plain encoding via handle.write(..., memory_aware=False). The writer sees zero Δ_j and c_j at the gate input. Memory writes still apply normally and delta encoding remains the default.
  • atomicng monitor produces standalone HTML with patch state, a row norm histogram, write metrics, and the verification result.
  • atomicng export-ple exports T⁰+Δ in the binary DNGPLE01 format with a JSON header, float32 rows, and SHA-256 integrity checks. The loader validates magic bytes, integrity, and the table specification.
  • The test count rose from 66 to 72.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • Resolve a circular import by reading the version lazily in monitor_html.py.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• paper.py centralizes paper constants, including 512/128 blocks, groups of 12, AdamW at 3e-4 with clip 1 and zero weight decay, ρ=0.01, 16 heads of width 160, approximately 4,075,681 writer parameters, and reference acquisition and retention figures.
  • Twelve conformance tests cover D1 equations, gate inputs, Equation 7 features, writer parameter count (±5% on the native configuration), ρ calibration, trainer and evidence defaults, and α=1. FIDELITY.md documents conformance, deviations, and the clean-room policy.
  • calibrate_to_table(t0) sets the writer target scale using ρ=0.01 and the base-table RMS.
  • Detached Ed25519 signatures for overlays and writer checkpoints through generate_keypair, sign_file, and verify_file. Integrity manifests detect corruption and signatures detect substitution.
  • The test count rose from 54 to 66.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • WriterMLP uses linear targets by default. Set bound_targets=True to enable tanh bounding. Writer artifacts preserve this setting across save and load.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• HFWriterTrainer trains a writer on a real Hugging Face model. The differentiable Δ injection sends gradients through the frozen model and projection to the writer. Loss uses cross-entropy over the block continuation. Groups without a gradient path are skipped.
  • SidecarHandle.nll reports mean NLL in nats per token under the current memory.
  • scripts/train_writer.py builds blocks, trains with BPTT, saves a safetensors checkpoint with model ID and corpus SHA-256, and evaluates acquisition on held-out documents.
  • The first AtomicNG writer checkpoint trained on SmolLM2-135M used a public-domain Gutenberg corpus and a small CPU configuration.
  • 54 tests, including real-model training, finite gradients, frozen model weights, checkpoint round-trip, and NLL changes after writing.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text: • Removed a no_grad scope that disconnected the writer from BPTT. Removed redundant dimension expansion of counts_t and Ĥ, whose hook already returns (B, T, Hd).

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Backend-independent acquisition (Δ_empty and Δ_donor), distraction (retention@k), and chain (neutral drift, recall, and stability) protocols. Each takes a patch snapshot and restores it after evaluation.
  • TinyModel.token_logits and TinyModel.nll.
  • Data-only safetensors writer artifacts with version and architecture validation, plus writer_fingerprint for SHA-256 provenance.
  • atomicng eval with quick, acquisition, distraction, and chain suites and optional JSON output.
  • The test count rose from 40 to 51. Coverage includes protocol state restoration, artifact round-trip and fingerprints, real Llama sidecar integration with bit-exact reset, and a positive Δ_empty test using a trained writer on the small PyTorch backend.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • The PyTorch extra now includes safetensors>=0.4.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • Renamed the prerelease project from dng to atomicng, including the import, CLI, overlay tag, and specification tag. References to the paper retain its original method name, Delta N-gram.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• WritePolicies with atomic row and write budgets and soft and hard norm caps. D1 calculates and validates proposed rows before applying them.
  • build_blocks with the paper's 512-token blocks and 128-token query prefix, plus ByteTokenizer.
  • A metrics registry with JSONL, TensorBoard, and W&B exporters for gates, norms, hot rows, row reuse, and events per second.
  • atomicng bench measures write throughput, read overhead, and verification time. check_regression supports CI.
  • atomicng publish checks verification, drift on neutral probes, and hot rows.
  • WriterMLP, TorchTinyModel, and WriterTrainer, with BPTT through D1, one backward pass per group, AdamW at 3e-4, clip 1, and a gradient stop at Ĥ. The Hugging Face sidecar injects reads before layer L and captures Ĥ.
  • SHA-256 overlay manifests, D1 merging, provenance, YAML configuration, typed package metadata, CI, and Ruff checks.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Verification and publication use probes that avoid patched rows.
  • D1 limits moved from D1Rule to WritePolicies.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• NumPy core with TableSpec, sparse MemoryPatch, lazy decay, snapshots, overlay round-trip, D1 block averaging, pre-image undo, audit logs, bit-exact deletion verification, TinyModel, and CLI smoke checks.
  • Property tests for convexity, boundedness, and within-block order invariance.

docs.title: AtomicNG conformance to the paper
docs.text: AtomicNG tracks conformance to Hao Wu's 2026 paper, Delta N-gram: Forward-Only Continual Writing into a Language Model's Native N-gram Memory (arXiv:2610.31125). paper.py holds the reference constants. The tests named below check the corresponding implementation where applicable.

docs.title: Clean-room implementation
docs.text: The project records that the upstream repository af-74413592/delta-ngram had no license when AtomicNG was implemented. The clean-room implementation used the paper and the upstream public README for documented behavior, CLI concepts, and smoke configuration. AtomicNG uses its own writer checkpoint and overlay formats.

docs.title: Conformance matrix
docs.text:
✓ matches the paper and has a test where applicable. ≈ has a documented deviation. ✗ marks an open gap. + marks an extension.

Item Paper AtomicNG Status Decomposition T = T⁰ + Δ T⁰ is frozen and Δ is sparse over touched rows. MemoryPatch stores only touched rows and has no write access to T⁰. ✓ (test_core, verify) D1 write rule A_j=(1/n)Σβ_a v_a, w_j=(1/n)Σβ_a, Δ⁺=(1−w)Δ+A, c⁺=c+1 per block (D1 averages a block's events into one update, so c_j counts writing blocks — confirmed by the author, issue #1 on the reference repo) rules/d1.py applies the rule in two phases with c_j += 1 per touched row per block. The test compares it directly with the equations. ✓ (test_fidelity::d1, test_counts_increment_per_block) Boundedness (Proposition 1) ‖Δ_j⁺‖ ≤ max(‖Δ_j‖, max‖v_a‖) Property test over a random chain of 50 blocks. ✓ (test_core::bounded) Within-block order invariance Block averaging is commutative. Property test compares checksums after shuffling events. ✓ (test_core::order) Gate β_a = σ(B_θ[x_a, Δ_j, v_a−Δ_j, log(1+c_j)]) WriterMLP.b_head uses F+2d+1 input features and a sigmoid. ✓ (test_fidelity::gate) Equation 7 features [Ĥ_p; mean p+1..p+4; block pool; (order, head) embedding], with gradients stopped at Ĥ WriterMLP.forward uses F=3·Hd+emb, detaches Ĥ, and sets FEATURE_NEXT_WINDOW=4. ✓ (test_fidelity::eq7) Writer architecture V_θ and B_θ are two-layer MLPs with hidden size 256 and about 4,075,681 parameters combined. The same formula is used. The native configuration differs by less than 1%. ✓ (test_fidelity::params) Target scale s_h Fixed s_h gives an initial target RMS of 0.01·RMS(T⁰_h). calibrate_to_table(t0, ρ=0.01) uses N(0,1) noise because the paper leaves the calibration input distribution unspecified. ≈ (test_fidelity::rho) Linear targets v = s_h·V_θ(x), without clipping bound_targets=False by default. The sidecar can opt into tanh stabilization. ✓/≈ (test_torch::tanh) Plain and delta encoding Plain (λ=0) encodes on the T⁰-only model: a four-stage training schedule (encode all blocks in one batch → D1 chain block-by-block → all queries forward+backward in one batch → backprop along the write chain) reaches ~3,200 target tokens/s vs ~940 interleaved, loss within 0.001 of sequential. Delta (λ=1) encodes with the memory written by earlier blocks; the delta writer is the plain writer forked at 80M tokens and fine-tuned with λ=1 for the last 20M. Delta-side BPTT is implemented in both trainers (memory-aware). At write time, handle.write(..., memory_aware=False) supplies zero Δ and c_j (plain encoding). The batched plain training schedule is the open gap — the larger gain is in training speed, not write-time. ≈ (test_v04::plain) Training blocks and query prefix 512 tokens per block and 128 query tokens build_blocks defaults to 512/128. Small CPU runs explicitly request shorter blocks. ✓/≈ (test_fidelity::evidence) Group normalization Normalize loss once per group of 12 trajectories. Group normalization is implemented. Group size is configurable and CPU runs use fewer than 12. ≈ Optimizer AdamW, LR 3e-4, no weight decay, clip 1 Both trainers use these defaults. ✓ (test_fidelity::hyper) BPTT through writes Backpropagate through the D1 chain to θ and stop gradients at Ĥ. Both trainers store differentiable Δ rows, backpropagate once per group, and skip groups without a gradient path. ✓ (test_hf_training) Empty starting memory Reset for each trajectory. Set self._delta = {} at the start of each trajectory. ✓ Predict before writing Algorithms 1 and 2 predict the block before writing it. Both trainers follow this order. ✓ Decay Δ ← αΔ Primary setting α=1, with 0.99 also evaluated using a block clock MemoryPatch(decay) applies lazy decay by clock tick and defaults to 1.0. ✓ (test_fidelity::evidence) Delete Δ to restore the base Clearing Δ restores the model. verify_deletion checks neutral probe outputs bit for bit and verifies the restoration checksum. ✓ (test_core) Native 16-head table 8 bigram heads, 8 trigram heads, d=160, with reads before layer 2 TableSpec supports this layout. The Track A sidecar uses one bigram head. Native model integration is tracked under Track B. ✗ for the full native path Paper-scale results Δ_empty 0.068/0.024, retention 54%/70%, 35,000 writes paper.py records the references. Full-scale reproduction remains open. ✗ Hot-row guard The paper observes formatting rows and analyzes the failure mode. guards adds norm caps and budgets, with hot-row metrics. + Publication checks Outside the paper's scope publish_check checks verification, drift, and hot rows. Artifacts support Ed25519 signatures. + Monitoring Outside the paper's scope MetricsRegistry and atomicng monitor produce a standalone HTML report with an SVG norm histogram. + Engine export Third-party vLLM patch export-ple writes the merged table in binary DNGPLE01 format with SHA-256 integrity for llama.cpp. Engine-side vLLM integration is Track B work. + Undo semantics The paper does not cover undo. + Pre-image journal; LIFO only — exact for the most recent block. Reverting an older block after later blocks touched the same rows is not exact (D1 depends on current row state). Documented in journal.py. + Reported acquisition numbers Δ_empty (0.068) and Δ_donor (0.024) are reported together: forgetting can raise Δ_donor by degrading the donor's memory. benchmarks.acquisition always returns both in one report. ✓

docs.title: Documented deviations
docs.text:
1. Track A attaches an external table with its own read projection (SidecarTable.proj). Track B covers integration with a model's built-in table. SmolLM2 sidecar results are external-table calibration (as the paper treats its prototype), not native-table results; the read projection is deterministic from seed 17 and ships with checkpoints (save_sidecar_proj).
  2. Small CPU runs explicitly use block lengths of 64–96, prefixes of 16–24, fewer than 12 trajectories per group, and a hidden size of 64 instead of 256. The paper defaults remain 512/128/3e-4.
  3. Tanh bounding is optional (bound_targets=True). The default targets are linear.
  4. Write-time plain encoding is implemented. Batched plain-writer training (four-stage schedule, ~3,200 target tokens/s) remains open.
  5. Target-scale calibration uses a noise probe because the paper does not specify the calibration input distribution.

docs.title: Updating this record
docs.text: When changing a listed feature, update its row and corresponding conformance test. Record any new deviation and its rationale. Run pytest tests/test_fidelity.py when reviewing conformance.

docs.title: AtomicNG and vLLM integration
docs.text: AtomicNG writes to a sparse overlay Δ while keeping the model weights and base n-gram table fixed. The effective table is T = T⁰ + Δ. This guide describes two integration paths and an upstream proposal.

docs.title: 1. Export a merged table
docs.text:
Export the full table and load it before inference:

pip install atomicng
atomicng write --evidence docs.txt --overlay mem.atomicng.npz
atomicng export-vllm --overlay mem.atomicng.npz --base-table t0.npz \
    --model-id Qwen3.8-Flash-Next --out ./vllm-artifacts
# Output: vllm-artifacts/ngram_table_merged.npz and vllm_config.json

The configuration records the merged table path, table dimensions and heads, SHA-256, and provenance. The runner loads the merged table before inference, so it does not apply the overlay on each read.

docs.title: 2. Use the general plugin
docs.text:
AtomicNG registers a vllm.general_plugins entry point. To supply an overlay when starting the server:

pip install atomicng
export VLLM_ATOMICNG_OVERLAY=/path/mem.atomicng.npz
vllm serve <model> ...

With no overlay configured, the plugin returns an empty dictionary. With an overlay, it provides atomicng_ngram_overlay(base_table, spec), which returns the merged table and its MemoryPatch.

docs.title: 3. Upstream Engram proposal
docs.text: For models with a built-in n-gram table, the proposal adds --ngram-overlay path to the existing Engram/PLE load path.

docs.title: Draft issue for vllm-project/vllm
docs.text:
Title: Feature: overlay support for n-gram/Engram sidecar tables (forward-only memory writes)

Body: AtomicNG (Apache-2.0, arXiv:2610.31125) implements forward-only continual writing into an n-gram sidecar table: pretrained table T⁰ stays frozen, new knowledge accumulates in a sparse patch Δ with block-averaged DeltaNet-style updates (convex combination ⇒ bounded norms), and clearing Δ restores the base model bit-exactly. Writes are forward-only (no gradients).

Proposal: allow serving with an n-gram overlay — --ngram-overlay path — that adds Δ on top of the factory table at load time. Artifacts are data-only safetensors/npz with sha256 manifests and provenance; a general-plugin entry point (vllm.general_plugins → atomicng_ngram_overlay) already ships in pip install atomicng and can supply the merged table (T⁰+Δ) to the engine. Calibration on SmolLM2-135M sidecar and a Tesla T4/Linux verification (72/72 tests, bit-exact restore) are published in the repo.

Use cases: continual knowledge updates without retraining; per-tenant memory overlays (merge/revert via pre-image journal); A/B of knowledge versions by swapping overlays.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text:
• The merged table uses little-endian float32 with shape (N, d), matching the overlay specification.
  • The plugin does not import vLLM. The plugin tests can run without it.
  • See CALIBRATION.md for the status of live vLLM calibration on Linux.
